newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower while pork bellies were called 0.250 to 0.500 cent per lb lower, livestock analysts said.

Carryover technical selling and fund liquidation coupled with steady to weak cash hog indications early were expected to weigh on hog futures. Wholesale pork is not moving at expected levels which is keeping packer bids down, analysts said.
Added pressure in deferreds could again stem from expectations that the next USDA Hogs and Pigs report will show stepped up hog production, they said.

Although losses were mostly pared in pork bellies late Monday by local short covering, carryover technical selling and recent weakness in cash bellies were expected to weigh on futures. Futures moved to lowest levels since mid-April before bouncing Monday, they said.

However, support could develop ahead of Tuesday's weekly CME Out-of-Town storage report. The report is expected to show an out-movement last week of between 0.5 to 1.0 million lbs versus an out-movement of 0.137 million and an in-movement of 0.428 million lbs last year, they added.
